gen-nixie-one-gf-source-sans-3: Hairline-thin strokes that never swell or thin out give Nixie One its wire-bent, retro-tech look. Source Sans 3 is the one that does the steady work, with an a whose lower bowl opens up to breathe.
gen-nixie-one-gf-special-gothic: Nixie One draws its open, nostalgic curves in a single unvarying line, and Special Gothic follows with rounded, inviting sans-serif letters. Shrink the heading and it thins out fast.
gen-nixie-one-gf-spinnaker: Wire-thin and retro, with curves left wide open. Nixie One sets the mood, and Spinnaker keeps its counters connected to the space outside.
gen-nixie-one-gf-stick: Nixie One has a constant stroke running from top to baseline, like bent wire. Stick takes over below with tubelike, constant-weight lines whose wide exits let light through, so a long block of text stays easy on the eye.
gen-nixie-one-gf-suse: Nostalgic in its open, wire-fine curves, Nixie One looks back while SUSE looks straight at you. And its rope-heavy curves and ladle-like open bowls make a longer sans passage feel friendly and unhurried.
gen-nixie-one-gf-suse-mono: SUSE Mono reads with extra room on both sides of every letter, and its open curves keep clear gaps throughout. Nixie One matches that openness, wearing it in a retro-tech outline.
gen-nixie-one-gf-tajawal: Nixie One traces every letter in one unbroken, constant line. Tajawal then carries a longer passage with a broad, open hook of a c, keeping the plain sans text clean and quiet.
gen-nixie-one-gf-tasa-explorer: Nixie One has no calligraphic swelling anywhere in its outlines, just a constant retro-tech stroke. But TASA Explorer adds the warmth, its curve ends stopping like brush strokes lifted early.
gen-nixie-one-gf-tasa-orbiter: TASA Orbiter reads clean, with an unclogged feel in every small counter. Nixie One, in neon-tube style constant strokes, gives the heading a retro-tech glow, while TASA Orbiter keeps long sans text clear.
gen-nixie-one-gf-teachers: Neon-thin and nostalgic, Nixie One keeps a constant stroke from top to baseline. Teachers answers in thin steel-rod sans-serif letters, where Nixie One shows off and Teachers simply reads.
